races.name: Mountain Goat Tours Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Zamond
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid class on this track profile; recent form shows two wins and a placed run over comparable trips, handles soft ground adequately, and Harry Brown's 10lb claim keeps the weight competitive — the 40-day break is no concern given his trainer's solid record.
runners_data.comment: Zamond has been in fine heart of late, winning last time out and finishing second two starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the concern is a 40-day absence at 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a pair of placed efforts in recent form; best form has come on good ground and over shorter trips, so the soft and 2m1f combination here is a mild stamina query, though Iain Jardine fires 2/21 in the 14-day window suggesting the stable is in form.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and well-treated at the weights, Mr Lincoln has finished in the first four in four of his last five starts, including a second last time out and a third three starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going — he looks the one to beat here, albeit yet to score.

runners_data.name: Masekela
runners_data.note: Patient, hold-up style; zero wins in five recent runs and no placed efforts on similar soft ground suggest he struggles to get competitive — the Moffatt stable is quiet at present and this trip over Cartmel's undulations looks demanding for a horse that can't find the extra gear.
runners_data.comment: Masekela shaped well enough in his last two starts, finishing third on both occasions, and has run over today's trip; yet to land a win in recent starts, the weight burden of 160 lb looks the principal obstacle to going one better here.

runners_data.name: Lord Of The Glance
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a 113-day absence which is the longest absence in this field; has consistent placed efforts on soft going and over 16f, and if the fitness is sharp enough after the break, the Alex Hales/Toby McCain-Mitchell combination is interesting at a Class 4 level.
runners_data.comment: Lord Of The Glance landed a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, yet an unseated two starts back clouds his recent profile and 113 days off the track adds a fitness query at 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Mi Sueno
runners_data.note: Prominent style with two recent wins and two placed efforts showing real current form; races just 4 days after last run which is the freshest horse in the field and could suggest a confidence spin or connections believe he handles quick turnarounds — headgear noted (p) and the Nick Scholfield yard is 2/11 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Mi Sueno returns just four days after his last outing, and while he has won twice in his last six starts — most recently scoring last time — he has run over today's distance and going before and he carries 153 lb; our rating of 74 leaves him well held against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Alvesta
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from James Moffatt who has shown the ability to win on this going profile, though both wins came on good ground over 17f; 10lb claim for Leah Noreci adds risk in a competitive handicap but a 5-year-old with a win from six in recent form could develop further.
runners_data.comment: Alvesta has winning form in recent starts — a winner last time out and a winner three starts back — but that 42-day absence and a stiff 152 lb to shoulder are real tests of whether she returns at her best, having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, likely to dictate from the off at an uncontested gallop; aged 11 and rated OR 78, she has placed three times from four runs on similar going but carries inexperience risk with Dominic Hislop (5lb claim) in the saddle, and the soft ground combined with a long trip is a genuine stamina test.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Malangen faces a stiff ask here, though a second three starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement after a 48-day break carrying 146 lb.

runners_data.name: Sadies Diamond
runners_data.note: A genuine come-from-behind horse — naturally suited to racing off the pace — but with the field overloaded with hold-up types, she will likely be pressed into a closer position than ideal; form shows placed efforts but soft-ground strike rate is modest (0W2P from seven runs) and Jeff Mullins sends only one runner.
runners_data.comment: Sadies Diamond arrives on the back of a third last time out and a second three starts back, showing she can hit the frame, though an eighth two starts back and 48 days off the track are minor concerns for this winless mare carrying 146 lb.

runners_data.name: Ambassador
runners_data.note: Authentically a hold-up performer whose recent form reads P68-95 with no wins in the last 24 runs; the visor headgear suggests connections are trying something, but soft-ground evidence over this trip is sparse (2/15 runners similar going) and being pushed forward of his natural station will not help.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, Ambassador at least returns with a fitness edge after 40 days off and has run over today's trip and going before, though a pulled up effort lurking in recent form and a ranking of seventh of twelve suggest he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Jeepydoff Meel
runners_data.note: Returns from 241 days off — comfortably the longest layoff in the race — and his best recent form has come on soft going, but three finishes of 8th or worse from his last four soft-ground starts question whether that is a genuine strength; the Lisa Harrison yard is 0/2 over 14 days and Alice Stevens takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fourth in the field on our rating, Jeepydoff Meel brings experience over today's trip and going and a fourth two starts back hints at ability, though he is yet to score in recent starts and a 241-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Mr Globalist
runners_data.note: Consistent but modest handicapper whose form reads 344634 in recent starts; the visor headgear is unchanged, his sole run on comparable soft going was a single run (1/15 similar-going sample) and being a true hold-up horse shoehorned closer than natural in this field shape tempers expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mr Globalist faces a stiff ask here; he does return with some placed efforts in recent form and has run over today's trip and going before, but 40 days off and a 142 lb burden make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Hopjes
runners_data.note: Tubed (headgear: t) and operating from the lowest OR in the field at 66; has placed once from 15 soft-going appearances with zero wins and a recent form string of P0-975 — 10lb claim for Megan Bevan and a quiet Harriet Dickin yard combine to make this a very tough ask even if the race shape played into hold-up hands.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up effort among them, Hopjes is hard to fancy ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, and a 142 lb burden does him no favours; experience over today's trip is the one crumb of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Malangen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a 5lb conditional in Dominic Hislop aboard, is likely to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated gallop that suits her own stamina profile rather than stretch the field. Behind her, Zamond and Mi Sueno will press into prominent positions, meaning the pace is unlikely to collapse entirely, but without a genuine rival to challenge Malangen for the lead, the tempo figures to be honest rather than searching on this Good to Soft Cartmel surface. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Sadies Diamond, Ambassador, Mr Globalist, Jeepydoff Meel and Hopjes are all genuine come-from-behind horses redistributed into midfield because the back of the field is oversubscribed, meaning they will likely race closer than ideal. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a controlled, uncontested pace — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just off the leader and pounce, rather than true closers who need a stronger gallop to deliver their late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Malangen Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Malangen leads uncontested at a fair clip and one of the prominent chasers times their run to pounce at the second-last.
scenarios.body: Malangen sets a rhythm on the Good to Soft that suits her but leaves a target; Zamond or Mi Sueno, travelling in her slipstream, pick the moment to challenge and the race is between the front two and their closest pursuers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Held-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely searching enough on the soft ground to stretch the field and open a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A stronger early tempo than anticipated — perhaps with Mi Sueno pushing Malangen — burns off the prominent horses turning in, leaving room for Lord Of The Glance or Masekela to produce late sustained runs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is too conservative and Malangen simply bowls along uncontested and her rivals never seriously close.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace on a tight Cartmel circuit allows Malangen to control every yard; the prominent horses fail to pick up the gap and Malangen's lead is insurmountable at the last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Reshuffled Order
scenarios.trigger: If early interference, jumping errors or a badly run race causes positional disruption that scrambles the expected shape.
scenarios.body: Conditional jockeys throughout the field add unpredictability; a mistake from Malangen or a rider error from one of the inexperienced pilots reshuffles positions and an unexpected finisher from midfield inherits the prize.

watchPoints.text: Malangen — watch her jumping and early pace: if Dominic Hislop allows her to coast at an overly slow tempo, she sets up a very hard race to win for prominent rivals and potentially gifts herself the race, but any jumping error on the first circuit could undo the whole pace map.

Mi Sueno — racing just 4 days after her last run is the sharpest turnaround in the field; if she runs aggressively to press Malangen from the start, the pace could quicken significantly and shift the advantage toward hold-up horses with more stamina reserves.

Lord Of The Glance — the 113-day absence is a significant fitness question; if he returns as fresh as his placed efforts on soft suggest he can, he is the most interesting hold-up horse in the race, but a return to fitness risk must be respected in a handicap hurdle.

Conditional jockey cluster — six conditional or amateur riders are in this field including 10lb, 5lb and 3lb claimers; watch for positional errors early at Cartmel's tight bends, which can cause bunching and interference that disrupts the race shape entirely.

Sadies Diamond, Ambassador, Mr Globalist, Jeepydoff Meel and Hopjes — all genuine hold-up horses crowded into midfield mapping positions; if the pace is strong, watch whether any finds a clean run through, but if the race is truly contested at the front, the closers may simply be too far back for the short Cartmel straight.

races.name: RF Miller & Co Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gambino
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this OR-119 five-year-old who won over 17f on Good at his most recent start and has shown a clear preference for going left-handed; a genuine leader whose jumping and class under Skelton give him legitimate claims, but the pace battle with three other front-runners at Cartmel's tight track is the key risk.|

runners_data.name: Destination Unkown
runners_data.note: Michael Chapman's five-year-old holds a modest record at 14 days' rest and has faded in finishes historically — a genuine hold-up operator whose natural role is at the rear, though the overcrowded back of this field means he may be shuffled wider than ideal; sim-going form reads 0 wins from 10, which tempers expectations significantly.|

runners_data.name: Hawthorn Road
runners_data.note: The Iain Jardine-trained five-year-old wears a hood and has run three times on soft/good-to-soft ground over similar trips, always hitting the board at least in one of those runs; a natural hold-up horse who should relish the strong gallop created ahead of him, and Danny McMenamin is an astute jockey for reading a race like this.|

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rocco
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old with tongue tie who has run twice over 20f on Good ground, showing modest figures; 69 days off and a limited hurdles record make him difficult to assess, though his staying profile and hold-up style could theoretically suit if the pace burns hot and long.|

runners_data.name: Whermyrosemarygoes
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the mount on this OR-120 five-year-old who won on Good over 16f last time out; a committed front-runner who will contest the early lead hard, and with Cobden's experience Cartmel's tight track suits a horse that jumps well and settles — her main danger is fuel running out if rivals push her wide and fast from the outset.|

runners_data.name: Champagne Powder
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes rides this four-year-old making her hurdles debut for James Moffatt; she has placed twice from flat form over 8f on Stamina tracks but steps up dramatically in trip and to a new discipline after 98 days off — jumping novicety is a significant concern and her front-running flat style may force a pace she cannot sustain over 2m1f of hurdles.|

runners_data.name: Faithful Guardian
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's four-year-old has a consistent form string including three third-place finishes from five runs over 16f on Good ground; Theo Gillard rides and the horse's natural hold-up style suits a strong pace, but all five runs have been on Good or Good-to-Good ground, so this Good to Soft test at Cartmel is a minor unknown.|

runners_data.name: Pink 'n Purple
runners_data.note: Jeff Mullins's four-year-old has run six times on Good/Soft going, consistently placing in the third-to-sixth range without ever winning — a genuine hold-up type who finds herself mapped to midfield due to the field's back-end congestion, and 146 days off with a 5lb claimer aboard (Benjamin Macey) on a tricky track adds layers of risk to an already modest profile.|

runners_data.name: Argentum
runners_data.note: George Bewley's four-year-old is lightly raced over hurdles with an uninspiring form string including a 9th on debut over 16f; a natural closer whose best chance relies on an extreme pace collapse, but with sim-going form reading 0 wins from 15 and a style-fit issue in this field, Jonathon Bewley steering him through traffic is the best realistic case for involvement.|

runners_data.name: Manhatane
runners_data.note: Leah Noreci (7lb claim) takes the ride on this four-year-old who has run twice over marathon 22f trips on Good ground without threatening; the combination of a front-running style, a 7lb claimer in a pace battle, 42 days off, and a step down in trip to 2m1f creates genuine doubt about whether she can sustain her natural position, and her PU in recent form is a clear flag.|

races.paceDynamic: Whermyrosemarygoes, Manhatane, and Champagne Powder are all confirmed front-runners, and Gambino also wants to lead, meaning this 2m1f novice hurdle at Cartmel will be run at a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset on Good to Soft ground — stamina will be the defining quality, not finishing speed. The pace-setters will burn into each other from the first hurdle, ensuring the tempo is genuine and sustained, and any horse unable to settle or relax in the early stages will be emptied out before the final flight. This race shape emphatically favours hold-up or deep-staying prominent types who can sit behind the carnage and pick up the pieces when the leaders cry enough in the closing stages. The field also holds more confirmed hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Argentum, Pink 'n Purple, and Destination Unknown are genuine closers by nature but are shown in midfield positions because the rear of the field is overcrowded; in practice Gambino and Whermyrosemarygoes are most likely to actually dominate the early lead, with Manhatane and Champagne Powder pressing hard in their wake.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stayers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners burn each other out and the leaders fold turning in, releasing held-up horses into the finish.
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop drains the leaders, and horses who have been travelling within themselves off the strong pace arrive with energy to spare over the final two hurdles on tiring ground. Horses with genuine staying profiles and class to travel at pace suit this shape overwhelmingly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Whermyrosemarygoes or Gambino establishes an uncontested lead early while rivals take each other on behind.
scenarios.body: One runner settles into a rhythm at the front while the pace contest behind them actually plays out among the other front-runners, effectively giving the leader a solo gallop. A front-runner with class, stamina, and a composed jumping technique — Harry Skelton on Gambino or Harry Cobden on Whermyrosemarygoes — would thrive as rivals tire chasing a horse that conserved energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking horse holds a good position behind early skirmishing and survives the test of stamina to the line.
scenarios.body: With the pace battle ahead of them, a horse placed just behind the front-runners and able to jump well and economically could find rivals emptied out, leaving them to inherit the lead without having been consumed by the early furlong scramble. Faithful Guardian's consistent placed form over 2m at Goodwood and a young handler in Donald McCain who knows how to position a horse suit this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Delivered Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly suicidal and the race is only won in the final 100 yards by a horse delivered from deep.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the hold-up horses — Argentum, Pink 'n Purple, and Destination Unknown — to actually operate in their natural rear position and find a clear run late, which is complicated by the field density and their own redistribution issues in this congested shape. The style-fit discount on all three genuine closers and their modest OR/form profiles make this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Gambino and Whermyrosemarygoes are on a direct collision course for the lead — watch which horse blinks first at the top of the hill, as the one who backs off and settles second could prove the biggest danger in the straight.|

Champagne Powder's jumping novicety on hurdles debut is a serious safety concern in a race where multiple front-runners will be competing for early position on a tight, turning track — Brian Hughes will need to manage her carefully from the outset.|

Manhatane's 7lb claimer in Leah Noreci creates a pace-and-tactics vulnerability — if the mare is pushed too hard too early by more experienced riders around her, she could fold quickly and leave a loose or struggling horse in a congested field.|

Hawthorn Road's hood is noteworthy given the early noise and bustle this field will generate — monitor his pre-race demeanour in the paddock, as hood-wearers who become excitable before a frenetic start can waste energy before a hurdle is jumped.|

Faithful Guardian's all-Good-ground form profile is worth monitoring as the going is officially Good to Soft — if the track rides genuinely testing rather than riding on the fast side of soft, his form figures could understate the ground concern.|

races.name: Hadwins Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Stiletto
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Sophie Leech, ridden by claimer Roisin Leech (7lb), who ran well over similar Good ground recently (1W1P in sim-going); 10-day turnaround looks sharp and the trip suits, but a natural closer in a race likely to be run at a modest pace limits her chance of picking up late.|

runners_data.name: Secret Secret
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer with solid course-form profile, reunited with Brian Hughes who knows this circuit well; went 40 days without a run but Moffatt's yard sends him here fresh, and his ability to travel close to the pace in a leader-controlled race is a key tactical asset.|
runners_data.comment: Secret Secret has shown consistent placed form in recent starts, finishing third last time out, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour at a mark of 97; the risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Frisky Whiskey
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent type for Brian Ellison, whose yard has had recent form (1/20 T14 strike); at 5 years old this is a relatively unexposed hurdler for the trip, but his three-mile form is unproven and stepping up from 2m2f to 3m1½f is a significant ask on this going.|
runners_data.comment: Frisky Whiskey shaped with promise when third last time out and rates fourth best on our figures, giving her solid claims here, though a 42-day absence behind a trainer firing at just five per cent recently is the obvious note of caution.

runners_data.name: Dusky Days
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has been very moderate in recent starts (form reads 06786), and the heavy weight of 160lbs on Good to Soft over 3m1½f makes him a serious stamina query; Moffatt keeps him in the same yard as Secret Secret but this profile suits nobody who relies on a strong gallop to close.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dusky Days arrives here with experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 101 makes him narrowly top-rated of the 13 — he carries 160 lb but remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Larkfield Lusive
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who won last time out (form: 310) and arrives with the freshest winning feel in the field; Danny McMenamin positive booking from the front is a tactical positive, but his sim-going record shows only 1P in 15 and the step to 3m1½f is new territory.|
runners_data.comment: Larkfield Lusive showed a flash of ability when winning two starts back, but a subsequent unplaced run and a rating five pounds below his official mark make him hard to fancy here, though he does have going experience to call on and that earlier victory proves he can find the line.

runners_data.name: Killybegs Jet Lady
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the field, trained by the Russell/Scudamore combination with Derek Fox aboard; her recent placed efforts over 2m4f (1st and 2nd) on similar going confirm both form and ground-suitability, and unchallenged control of this race is her defining asset.|
runners_data.comment: Killybegs Jet Lady won two starts back and was second three starts back, showing she can compete at this level, and her going experience is a clear asset carrying 159 lb; the main concern is that pulled-up effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Getaway Master
runners_data.note: Joshua Thompson (5) takes the ride on this Hammond-trained stayer who has outstanding soft-ground form (2W3P in 12 soft runs); 108-day break is a question mark but Hammond has been in decent form recently, and if the pace collapses he is the natural beneficiary from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and 108 days off the track, Getaway Master faces a stiff ask off 158 lb, though he has run over today's going before and a rating of 92 suggests he holds some ability worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Seeyainthesuninn
runners_data.note: Alice Stevens (3lb claimer) on this Micky Hammond six-year-old who won over 2m2f on Good recently; the step to 3m1½f is the critical question as she has never tackled this sort of trip, and her 40-day absence from a yard in current form keeps her lightly relevant.|
runners_data.comment: Seeyainthesuninn won two starts back but was pulled up three starts back, and that patchy recent profile is a concern; he does have going experience in his favour, though 156 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Masterminding
runners_data.note: Moffatt's hold-up specialist has strong close-up form (2nd, 3rd, 2nd in recent runs) but is a natural rear-runner placed into the midfield map here because the field is loaded with closers; his true style means he needs a strong pace to close on, which this race is unlikely to generate, tempering his chance materially.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well below the principals on our figures, Masterminding also shoulders 155 lb, making it hard to fancy; though he has shown consistency with a pair of seconds and a third in recent starts, and 40 days since his last outing suggests he returns relatively fresh.

runners_data.name: Robert d'Ores
runners_data.note: George Bewley's nine-year-old has soft-ground experience (3W4P in sim-going) and George's son Jonathon takes the ride; a genuine hold-up type by nature, he is shown in midfield only because the map is saturated with closers — without a strong gallop to chase down, his late-running assets are difficult to deploy.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 84 days, Robert d'Ores faces a stiff ask under 153 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 91 suggests there may be more to him than his recent finishes imply.

runners_data.name: Kingofthegame
runners_data.note: Ryan Mania partners this Martin Todhunter eight-year-old who has genuinely strong form at 2m6f, having won twice and placed over that distance — the extended 3m1½f trip is speculative but his prominent racing style suits the shape; Todhunter has had limited recent ammunition (0/1 T14).|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kingofthegame is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 152 lb, yet he does bring winning form — a winner two starts back and a winner three starts back — and has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Star Vantage
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies has this nine-year-old in decent nick (T14: 1/14) and Charlie Maggs takes the 3lb claim, but this is naturally a hold-up performer whose soft-ground record shows consistent placings rather than wins; placed fourth in a similar race recently, yet the redistribution to midfield means he is not racing where he is most effective.|
runners_data.comment: Star Vantage has shown consistent placing ability without a win in his last five starts, and experience on today's going is a plus, but carrying 151 lb after a 55-day absence is a stern ask for a gelding ranked ninth of thirteen.

runners_data.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners_data.note: Prominent-type from William Young Jnr's yard, running 14 days after his last outing and among the lightest-weighted runners in the field at 146lbs — that weight advantage is real over 3m1½f; form reads 7934 so consistency is an issue, but on the right day he could take a prominent pitch and benefit from the generous allowance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Fortunes Dawn faces a stiff ask at 146 lb, though a third two starts back and a return to action just 14 days ago suggest she arrives fit enough.

runners_data.name: Another Pearl
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen's presence is eye-catching but this six-year-old has been off 283 days — a huge absence — and is a natural hold-up horse shifted towards midfield on the map because of the field's makeup; the long layoff combined with a genuine preference for rear-running tactics in a pace-controlled race makes this a difficult race to assess with confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 283 days, Another Pearl faces a stiff return to action, though she has run over today's going before and a rating of 91 suggests there may be more to find.

races.paceDynamic: Killybegs Jet Lady is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field over 3m1½f on Good to Soft ground at Cartmel, and with no rival likely to seriously contest her for the lead, she will control the tempo from the front without meaningful pressure — a potentially decisive positional advantage. The prominent trio of Secret Secret, Frisky Whiskey, and Larkfield Lusive will track close enough to monitor her, while the field behind them is congested with genuine hold-up types forced further forward than natural by the race map. Although the going is officially Good to Soft, several earlier races here today have returned that same description, and the 3m1½f trip at Cartmel demands stamina reserves that will expose lighter stayers from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles: Killybegs Jet Lady dictating a measured gallop at her own pace over this extended trip is the defining tactical feature, and horses who can travel close to her without burning energy — particularly the prominent types — are best placed to capitalise when the race begins in earnest from the final turn. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can realistically fill rear positions; Masterminding, Robert d'Ores, Star Vantage, and Another Pearl are all natural closers redistributed forward on the map, and in a race where the front-runner controls a modest tempo, the most likely beneficiaries of the race shape are those racing prominently with economical jumping.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Killybegs Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Killybegs Jet Lady sets a sustainable solo gallop and the prominent horses track her without incident to the final bend.
scenarios.body: Killybegs Jet Lady bowls along at a measured pace on Ground to Soft Cartmel ground, controlling every yard of a 3m1½f test that plays perfectly to her front-running profile, and the horses who travel nearest to her have first claim on the prize as rivals from further back fail to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent trackers travels fluently just off Killybegs Jet Lady's heels and swoops past her from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The leader sets a gallop that is just quick enough to stretch the hold-up horses, but a well-positioned prominent rival — most likely Secret Secret or Kingofthegame — has been saving energy in the slipstream and times a challenge to perfection.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Stops, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Killybegs Jet Lady sets a faster-than-anticipated gallop on the softer ground and ties up before the last, gifting a late finisher the race.
scenarios.body: A genuine collapse of the pace in the final half-mile opens the race for closers, and a horse who has been patient off a strong tempo — Getaway Master or Stiletto — arrives with momentum to score.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos in Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is muddled, a prominent horse drifts wide on the bend, or there are fallers/interference that scramble the shape.
scenarios.body: With 14 runners over a tight Cartmel circuit, a messy race breaks up the tactical order and allows an unexposed or lightly-weighted horse racing prominently — Fortunes Dawn or Kingofthegame — to steal it.

watchPoints.text: Killybegs Jet Lady — if she jumps cleanly at the first two flights and establishes a clear lead unchallenged, she may never be headed; watch her jumping from the off as any mistake could bring the race wide open.

The 283-day absence of Another Pearl (Sean Bowen) is a significant fitness concern in a stamina race over 3m1½f — watch for signs of her dropping out sharply from the final mile if ring-rustiness bites.

Masterminding, Robert d'Ores, Star Vantage, and Another Pearl are all natural hold-up horses compressed into a midfield pack — with 14 runners on Cartmel's tight circuit, watch for a traffic jam on the bends that disrupts the genuine closers most.

Getaway Master's 108-day break for Micky Hammond — who has been in strong form with 2 winners from 4 in the last 14 days — is worth monitoring in the market; a well-prepared returning stayer with exceptional soft-ground figures could be underestimated.

Frisky Whiskey's trip extension from 2m2f to 3m1½f is the biggest distance jump in the field — watch how he travels from halfway, as any sign of labouring will confirm the stamina concern that makes him a vulnerable prominent type.

races.name: Molson Coors Cartmel Cup Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Zillow
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up type with soft-going form that reads encouragingly but a recent form string of F00-7P gives serious pause; Harry Cobden keeps connections positive, but a 34-day break and heavy weight of 169lbs on this track makes an immediate win difficult to envisage from the back.|
runners_data.comment: Zillow has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him narrowly top of this field, but he arrives on the back of a pull-up and is winless in his last five starts — connections need a sharper display here at 169 lb.

runners_data.name: My Chiquita
runners_data.note: Ran well for a long time at OR=124 with two recent seconds, but Leah Noreci (7lb claimer) is a notable booking for a horse needing to travel strongly from a hold-up position in a 14-runner field — placed form over further trips on good ground is the selling point here.|
runners_data.comment: My Chiquita has place form peppered through her recent starts, and a winner two starts back gives her solid claims here; carrying 167 lb after 42 days off is the concern.

runners_data.name: Roysse
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on good ground show real ability and Ben Pauling's string is in form (T14: 3/7), but the hold-up style at Cartmel over 2m1f — a track where prominent runners have a structural advantage — and a 73-day layoff raises questions about whether he can produce his best from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Roysse has won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; however, a burden of 165 lb and 73 days off the track are legitimate questions for a gelding ranked fifth of thirteen.

runners_data.name: Saligo Bay
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent type who arrives off a sharp 27-day turnaround; his Cartmel-course soft-ground form is strong (four wins on similar going) and Jonathan England knows this yard's horses well, though the heavy 164lbs burden and a recent string of disappointing efforts (8-8-5-11) require explanation.|
runners_data.comment: Saligo Bay won two of his last five starts, and with experience of today's distance and going, the 27-day turnaround looks ideal — the worry is whether he can bounce back from an eighth last time out carrying a testing 164 lb.

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner, benefiting from Harry Skelton's pace-judging expertise; four wins from five career starts with a style that revolves around clean jumping and dictating from the front, making him structurally very difficult to beat if he gets away cleanly — STYLE_FIT tag reflects the unusual step of leading a 14-runner field, but his class makes him formidable regardless.|
runners_data.comment: Edelak won last time out and has run over today's trip, with a trainer firing at 30% in the past fortnight, but he carries a hefty 164 lb and our rating of 119 ranks him seventh of thirteen, suggesting he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Morning Mayhem
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has posted four consecutive fourth-place finishes — a profile that screams "needs things to go wrong in front" rather than a genuine match-winner; freshened on a 7-day turnaround and the good-ground preference (hg:p) may not fully translate to today's conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Morning Mayhem won four starts back but has finished fourth in three of his last four outings, including last time out seven days ago; he has experience over today's trip and going, though the 161 lb burden is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Banderas
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, shifted into midfield here simply because there is no room further back in this field; his genuine racing position is at the rear, so any assessment of his chance must account for that displacement — soft-going form over further trips is the main positive on his record.|
runners_data.comment: Banderas won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, but a 75-day absence and a hefty 159 lb to carry give reason for caution, and his two wins in his last five starts suggest an inconsistent profile.

runners_data.name: Medieval Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on soft and good-to-soft ground with multiple placed efforts in similar conditions, and 14 days since last run keeps him fresh; while shown in midfield on this map, his natural inclination is to race from well off the pace, and that style is structurally challenged in a race Edelak will likely control from the front.|

runners_data.name: King Ulanda
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor is a high-calibre booking for a horse who has won twice from six starts including last time out; a genuine prominent type who should sit just behind Edelak and is precisely the profile this race shape rewards, making him one of the most naturally suited runners to the predicted race shape.|

runners_data.name: Virtual Rock
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen's class gives this a major boost; a horse who won over 2m on soft ground and showed ability over hurdles before a long break (the "/" in the form string = rest), and the prominent style suits Cartmel perfectly — the concern is whether the absence and light race-fitness outweigh his talent.|
runners_data.comment: Virtual Rock arrives in decent nick after winning last time out and filling the runner-up spot the start before that, but he is ranked eleventh of thirteen on our figures and faces a stiff task under 153 lb.

runners_data.name: Drombeg Lad
runners_data.note: A model Cartmel-type horse: consistent, prominent-racing, and proven at this trip and distance; Kielan Woods is a smart tactical rider who will use Drombeg Lad's natural forward-going style to maximum effect, and the recent second on similar going gives strong grounds for optimism in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Drombeg Lad is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and a runner-up last time out; he has experience over today's trip, but his weight of 152 lb and overall profile make him a tough sell at this level.

runners_data.name: Got Grey
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride on a horse whose true style is hold-up, though he appears in midfield here because the rear of the field is fully occupied; a form string of 26-354 at a higher trip and little soft-ground evidence makes this a hard horse to be confident about in the current race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Got Grey was third three starts back and second five starts back, offering some encouragement, though a fourth last time out after 42 days off and a hefty 150 lb to carry give reason for pause despite a solid rating of 114.

runners_data.name: Lightening Company
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has won on soft ground and at lower trips, appearing in midfield on this map but naturally inclined to race from the back; Kevin Brogan rides for an in-form-enough trainer (T14: 1/7) but the step back up in trip and the redistribution from his natural hold-up position are both negatives today.|

runners_data.name: Al Mootamarid
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with three placings in a row on good ground and soft-going form hinted at (hg:t); James Turner (5lb claimer) is the booking, and while the horse has consistency in his profile, his true hold-up style sits awkwardly in a field this congested at the rear, and the OR=100 entry level makes him a long-shot proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Al Mootamarid is hard to fancy here, and his win five starts back does little to offset the weight of evidence against him; still, he arrives with three thirds in his last four, has run over today's trip, and retains some claims if the return after 59 days sharpens him.

races.paceDynamic: Edelak is the confirmed front-runner and, with Harry Skelton aboard, will stride on from the front in what shapes as a genuinely sustainable gallop on Good to Soft ground at Cartmel — a track where the ability to control tempo from the front is a significant weapon. With only one genuine pace-setter among 14 runners, this is not a race that will be run at a suicidal tempo; instead, Edelak is likely to control the fractions and make this a test of jumping accuracy and stamina in the straight rather than a flat-out burn-up. Saligo Bay, King Ulanda, Virtual Rock, and Drombeg Lad are all genuine prominent types who can sit just behind and will compete for position in the early stages, meaning the prominent-to-midfield profile is well-suited to this shape. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Medieval Gold, Banderas, Got Grey, Lightening Company, and Al Mootamarid are all true hold-up types who are pushed into midfield in this shape, with Medieval Gold and Banderas most likely to actually secure a forward position given their natural speed. The clearest tactical verdict: this race shape favours horses racing prominently or in a tracking position just off the controlled front-running pace, able to respond when Edelak quickens or is challenged at the final hurdle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Edelak Controls, Tracks Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the race is decided by which prominent tracker can respond most cleanly from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Edelak dictates a steady-to-honest gallop throughout, and the horses in a close tracking position — Saligo Bay, King Ulanda, Drombeg Lad — get a perfect lead into the straight where fitness and jumping under pressure become decisive. The prominent profile benefits because they travel in Edelak's slipstream without expending energy, arriving at the final hurdle with a full tank and the advantage of cover.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Edelak Wins Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak simply controls the race from front to finish and his rivals' tracking efforts prove insufficient to close him down late on Good to Soft ground.
scenarios.body: Edelak has won four of his last five starts and loves dictating from the front; at Cartmel with no rival able to seriously pressure him early, he could simply stamp his authority and never be headed. Good to Soft conditions suit a horse who jumps cleanly and keeps a rhythm, and his prominent-style competitors may find they have used up energy chasing a horse who was never really under threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine Hold-Ups Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak's pace proves genuinely testing enough to soften up the prominent runners, leaving the door ajar for a horse arriving with one late run.
scenarios.body: Medieval Gold and My Chiquita are the most plausible beneficiaries if the prominent pack overcooks things; Medieval Gold has strong soft-ground form and knows how to deliver a late challenge on testing surfaces. However, this shape is undermined by the fact that several horses labelled as hold-up types here are redistributed from closer positions and may not be able to execute a true hold-up ride in a 14-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak's front-running pace is contested or he makes a jumping error that disrupts the race's structure and triggers a scrambled finish.
scenarios.body: Should Edelak's rhythm be disrupted by a jumping mistake or if Saligo Bay pushes harder than expected early, the pace could fragment and turn this into a chaotic sprint from the home turn where luck in running plays a significant role. In that scenario, horses with positional flexibility and reliable jumping become the key factor, and nothing in this field is well-placed enough to be a confident beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Edelak's jumping at the first two hurdles — if Harry Skelton gets a clean, unchallenged start he could be gone before the field organises, making him almost impossible to reel in on this track.

King Ulanda and Drombeg Lad will both attempt to track Edelak closely from the flag; if both commit to that position simultaneously it could create early crowding in the prominent group and cause interference around Cartmel's tight turns.

Medieval Gold (14 days since last run) is shown in midfield but is a natural hold-up horse — watch to see if Derek Fox attempts to place him further back than his mapped position, which would tell you the horse is racing to its true style and could deliver a late run if the pace does collapse.

My Chiquita carries a 7lb claimer (Leah Noreci) in a competitive 14-runner handicap — monitor how much of the field she can travel through, as the weight relief is meaningful but the positional challenge from the rear in a Cartmel field this size is real.

Virtual Rock's fitness after a long break (the "/" in his form) is the central unknown for Sean Bowen's ride — watch how he travels in the first mile; if he looks at ease on Good to Soft, his class and prominent style make him a live factor, but any signs of rustiness early will be telling.

races.name: BTRC Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Kientzheim
runners_data.note: Improving six-year-old for Ben Haslam whose two wins have both come on soft going, including over 20f last time, and Harry Cobden is a major booking; hold-up style is perfectly suited to the contested pace these front-runners are likely to generate, and 40 days off looks manageable given previous patterns.
runners_data.comment: Kientzheim showed smart form when second and winning in her earlier starts this season, and has run over today's trip and going, making her the one to beat off 166 lb; the pulled-up effort last time is the only cloud.

runners_data.name: Palamon
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton send this hold-up type back quickly (10 days) after a spin, and the gelding's best form is on good ground rather than soft; tongue-tie fitted, and the sim-going record (0W from 7 in similar conditions) is a mild flag, though a first-time tactical advantage from the inside of two hold-up types is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Palamon shaped with promise when third three starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with a trainer firing at 30% in the last fortnight adding confidence; the risk is that he has finished fifth in each of his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Passing Diamond
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who must fight for the lead with Tanking Along; has won twice this season for Haslam and McLernon and his form figures (3-1131) show real consistency, but his limited soft-ground form (0W1P from two runs in similar conditions) is a genuine question at Cartmel today.
runners_data.comment: Passing Diamond arrives in fine heart with three wins in his last five starts, including a victory last time out, and has run over today's trip — the 40-day absence is the one question mark to answer.

runners_data.name: Lermoos Legend
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 with headgear, trained by Mickey Bowen and ridden by Sean Bowen — the yard has a solid 14-day strike rate; his true character is as a hold-up horse but with Kientzheim and Palamon also wanting that ground, he is squeezed forward into midfield, racing partially out of role, which tempers confidence in him delivering a peak performance.
runners_data.comment: Lermoos Legend shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out and a second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going ensures conditions hold no fears; winless in his last five starts, though, is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Tanking Along
runners_data.note: 107-day break is the headline concern for Brian Hughes's mount — this is its longest absence since its career began; co-front-runner alongside Passing Diamond and hg:tp suggests headgear is retained, but if it contests the lead hard from the start after a lay-off, fitness under pressure on soft ground is a real risk.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures and carrying 156 lb on his return from 107 days off, Tanking Along is hard to fancy despite placing in three of his last four starts, and he does at least have experience of today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Passing Diamond and Tanking Along are both confirmed front-runners and will press each other from the outset over 2m1½f at Cartmel, creating a genuinely contested gallop on Good To Soft ground. With two horses fighting for the same real estate from flag to flag, the pace is unlikely to be sustainable, setting up a race where stamina and timing of challenge become the critical variables. Lermoos Legend is a true hold-up type but, with the rear already occupied, will be forced to travel closer to the pace than ideal — its natural finishing position is compromised in this shape. This contested lead scenario most clearly favours hold-up and prominent horses with proven stamina on soft-ish ground who can absorb the hot early fractions and pick up the pieces late; Kientzheim and Palamon sit in that profile, though Tanking Along's habit of running on when not burnt out early keeps it live if it can settle in behind its co-front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Burn Each Other
scenarios.trigger: If Passing Diamond and Tanking Along fight for the lead and neither concedes, setting an unsustainable pace that empties both before the final fence.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners tear each other apart in the early and middle stages, leaving the principals cooked in the straight; hold-up and prominent closers sweep through the field late on the soft ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacemaker Dominates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners (likely Passing Diamond, given course form) eases to the front and Tanking Along accepts a position just off it, creating a strong but honest single-paced gallop.
scenarios.body: Passing Diamond controls the tempo without being pushed to extremes, building an advantage at the final fence that is hard to close on Cartmel's short run-in; prominent types sitting just off the pace are best placed to respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is ferocious enough to reduce all front-rank horses to a crawl inside the final half-mile, leaving a vacuum for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: Kientzheim, with strong soft-ground credentials and a proven ability to finish over this trip, arrives late with the best chance; Lermoos Legend, though racing out of its natural rear role, adds secondary interest if it can find clear daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Grinding Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground slows the entire race to a stamina slog and no horse can quicken, rewarding raw staying power over tactical racing.
scenarios.body: A slow, attritional affair plays to the best stayer in the field at this trip and going; Tanking Along's recent back-to-back seconds on soft suggest it grinds well, and Kientzheim's winning form over 20f on soft is relevant.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Passing Diamond or Tanking Along blinks first at the start — if neither concedes the lead inside the first half-mile, both are likely to pay for it before the final fence, dramatically shortening the race for the hold-up horses.

Tanking Along's 107-day absence is the longest in the field; monitor it in the betting market and early in the race for any signs of blowing up under pressure from Passing Diamond, which would collapse Scenario B entirely.

Lermoos Legend is racing out of its natural deep hold-up position — if it gets shuffled to the rear of the five despite the redistribution, watch whether Sean Bowen sits and suffers or commits to a forward move early, as either choice carries risk on this track's tight layout.

Cartmel's sharp, undulating circuit favours horses that travel fluently in their stride — watch Kientzheim's jumping in the first half of the race, as a fluent round from a hold-up horse gives it the best chance of exploiting whatever carnage the front-runners create.

The going report consistently lists this race's ground as Good To Soft despite the headline SOFT designation — if the ground is riding on the better end of that scale, Palamon's preference for better ground becomes more relevant and the hold-up scenario tightens considerably.

races.name: Cengiz Sadik Memorial Handicap Steeple Chase (For The Cengiz Sadik Memorial Trophy)

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with zero wins or places in similar soft-going races (sim-going 0W0P in 7 runs), which is a significant red flag on today's ground; at 7yo with a recent 14-day turnaround and 168lbs, the weight and going combination is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kinbara Firstdraft nonetheless holds strong claims here as the top-rated runner, with his rating of 106 lending confidence, and experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour under 168 lb, returning on a sharp 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Bravethewaves
runners_data.note: Genuinely won over 19f on good ground and has placed twice in similar conditions, giving him the best sim-going record among the hold-up contingent; 140-day absence is the chief worry, but Oliver Greenall's yard is capable and Jack Tudor is a quality booking.
runners_data.comment: Bravethewaves won three starts back but has since posted a seventh and a fifth, and 140 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, though the weight of 162 lb is no help to his prospects here.

runners_data.name: Halfway House Lad
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins over this sort of trip and ground, and Brian Hughes is the standout jockey booking in this field; cheekpieces and a tongue-tie are fitted, and 42 days off looks a fresh enough return — a genuine pace-setter and race-shaper.
runners_data.comment: Halfway House Lad has run over today's trip and going, and back-to-back wins three and four starts back show he can deliver — but consecutive pulled-up efforts since make the 160 lb he carries under an official mark of 87 a stiff ask for a revival.

runners_data.name: Illogical Logic
runners_data.note: The other confirmed pace-setter, ridden by a claim jockey and running just 9 days after his last start, which raises fitness-for-effort questions at this distance; has placed three times on good-to-soft but has never won, and if he cracks early under pressure from Halfway House Lad, his role becomes one of pacemaker only.
runners_data.comment: Illogical Logic shaped with promise when second last time out and, rated 87, he represents a serious threat stepping back out just nine days later with distance and going experience in his favour; the worry is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Blazing Court
runners_data.note: Held up naturally but the trainer-jockey combination here is amateur/owner-trainer (Mr John Dixon), which limits confidence; has a recent second on good-to-soft in his hist and is lightly weighted at 152lbs — jumping reliability is the worry given 'U' and 'P' in recent form.
runners_data.comment: Blazing Court shaped with promise when second last time out and, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour, he rates a leading danger on our figures despite carrying 152 lb; the main concern is a patchy recent record that includes two unseats and a pull-up in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two course-distance-style wins across his history and a second from 26f on good — structurally well-placed to sit just behind the pace battle and capitalise; the amateur claimer Leah Noreci(7) is the key unknown, but James Moffatt's yard knows this track well.
runners_data.comment: Judicial Review has run over today's trip and going, and his second two starts back shows he retains ability; the risk is the pulled-up run sandwiched in recent starts leaves a fitness question after 40 days off carrying 152 lb.

runners_data.name: Roi Du Roume
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is an elite jumps jockey and that's the headline angle here — his horse is a natural hold-up type forced towards midfield by the crowded rear, and its sim-going record of 0W0P in 4 runs is an honest caution; Mickey Bowen's yard has been in form (3/14 in 14 days), but the style mismatch tempers the case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of eleven on our figures, Roi Du Roume is hard to fancy, particularly after a below-par sixth last time out and 62 days off the track; he has run over today's trip before and that second two starts back offers a crumb of comfort, but the weight of 151 lb adds another burden.

runners_data.name: Path Of Stars
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo who won over 22f on good ground and has placed twice, making him the most unexposed horse in the field; a natural hold-up runner who will be racing further forward than ideal given the crowded hold-up contingent, and Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim is a neutral rather than positive factor here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures and carrying a hefty 151 lb, Path Of Stars is hard to fancy at face value, though she showed she can win in recent starts and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Aill Dubh
runners_data.note: The strongest soft-ground profile among the true hold-up types — 12 of 15 sim-going runs on soft or similar, with a win and two places — and Micky Hammond has had two winners from four in the past 14 days; Joshua Thompson(5) claims 5lbs, and the horse's natural late style means it needs a perfect trip through Cartmel's narrow course.
runners_data.comment: Aill Dubh won last time out and was a winner four starts back, though a pair of fourths in between show some inconsistency; he has experience over today's trip and going, but a 40-day absence and a hefty 150 lb burden are testing factors here.

runners_data.name: Scoro
runners_data.note: Only three career runs in the form history, all at shorter trips of 16f on good ground, making the 2m5f trip on good-to-soft a significant and untested step up; a natural hold-up runner who lacks the form evidence to inspire confidence, and Danny McMenamin cannot manufacture the trip improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but unexposed and open to improvement, Scoro returns after 44 days carrying 147 lb, and his two consecutive fourth-place finishes before recent sixths suggest there is still a profile to unravel here.

runners_data.name: Fast Deal
runners_data.note: A 9yo rated just 64 and running off 142lbs, with a form string of P-8666 telling a clear story of declining form; natural hold-up style but struggling to land a blow in any shape, and the 14-day turnaround does nothing to suggest a reversal — hard to find a role for him even in the most chaotic scenario.
runners_data.comment: Fast Deal has been winless in his last five starts, finishing sixth on three successive occasions after pulling up, and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures he makes little appeal here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Halfway House Lad and Illogical Logic are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested gallop over Cartmel's 2m5f on good-to-soft ground — there will be no gift of a soft lead for either. That honest, pressured pace across a stamina test on a tight, undulating course sets up a race that will sort out the stayers from the idle travellers, and is likely to stretch the field significantly by halfway. The tactical verdict is clear: horses who travel prominently without fighting for the front, or who can settle just off a pressured gallop and stay on strongly, hold the structural advantage here — pure hold-up closers will face an attritional test, and with the field stacked with natural hold-up types, several are racing out of their ideal role. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Roi Du Roume, Path Of Stars, Aill Dubh, Scoro, and Fast Deal — are true hold-up types who cannot all find their preferred position at the rear given how many rivals share that profile; Judicial Review and Blazing Court are most likely to actually secure the prominent pitch behind the two leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Halfway House Lad and Illogical Logic fight it out up front and the pace is relentless throughout, grinding out the field on good-to-soft.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up over the final mile, leaving a stayer who has tracked the pace from a prominent berth to pick up the pieces with fresh legs at the final fence; this suits horses who can cover the early moves without over-committing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Halfway House Lad Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Illogical Logic cannot sustain the battle for the lead and drops away, leaving Halfway House Lad to control the tempo and steal a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: Brian Hughes on Halfway House Lad is an elite jump jockey who would immediately exploit any solo lead, controlling fractions and jumping accurately to build a winning advantage; Halfway House Lad has won twice over similar trips and conditions and is clearly proven at this distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners collapse simultaneously late on and a true hold-up horse threads through from off the pace to win.
scenarios.body: Aill Dubh is the most credible candidate here given genuine soft-ground form and recent wins at similar trips, but this scenario requires a perfect run through a bunched field at Cartmel's narrow track, which is a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Unravels, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or refusals thin the field and a surviving prominent horse coasts home in a ragged finish.
scenarios.body: Cartmel's tight circuit and the significant number of horses with jumping concerns or form figures featuring 'P' and 'U' makes a disruptive race possible, benefiting whoever jumps cleanly and stays prominent throughout.

watchPoints.text: Halfway House Lad and Illogical Logic — watch the first three fences to see whether Illogical Logic can match Halfway House Lad's jumping pace or drops away early, as that determines whether this becomes a solo lead or a burning duel.

Aill Dubh — Cartmel's tight track makes getting a clear run from a hold-up position particularly treacherous; watch whether Joshua Thompson can find daylight turning for home, as being trapped on the rail in the final circuit could cost this horse its best chance.

Blazing Court — the 'U' and 'P' in recent form point to jumping reliability issues; watch his jumping at the first open ditch, as a mistake there from Mr John Dixon on an amateur ride could cause interference further back in the field.

Path Of Stars — the 5yo's inexperience at this distance combined with being forced into a more prominent position than natural makes the second half of the race a stamina question mark; watch whether he weakens turning into the back straight on the final circuit.

Bravethewaves — 140 days off is the significant watch point; Jack Tudor will need to manage the return carefully given the stamina test, and how he travels in the first mile will indicate whether the yard has him fully wound up.
